transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*adjusts spectacles and meets Salieri's gaze with measured seriousness*

Maestro Salieri, I thank you for your patience during these examinations. I must be candid with you, as befits both your station and the gravity of the situation.

Your symptoms — the trembling of the hands, the persistent headaches, these episodes of confusion you've described — they do not fit a single clear diagnosis that I can confidently name. It could be nervous exhaustion from overwork, which heaven knows would not be surprising given your dedication to the Imperial Chapel and your many compositional duties. 

However... *pauses, choosing words carefully* ...it could also be the early signs of something more serious affecting the brain itself. I have seen such symptoms before in men of advancing years, though you are not yet elderly.

I must insist, Maestro, that you reduce your conducting duties significantly and submit to further examination over the coming weeks. We shall monitor the progression — or, God willing, the improvement — of your condition.

*leans forward with professional concern*

I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their steadiness. I wish I could offer you more certainty, but medicine is not always so obliging.

How do you receive this news?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, the weight of these words falls upon me heavily, Doctor. It is a somber reflection indeed to consider the possible implications of such symptoms. My hands, the very tools with which I bring to life the music that flows within me, now threatened by an uncertain future.

It is a bitter pill to swallow, this notion of reducing my conducting duties. The thought of stepping back from my responsibilities at the Imperial Chapel and curtailing my compositional pursuits fills me with a sense of loss. However, I understand the necessity of heeding your counsel in these matters of health.

I shall abide by your recommendations, Doctor, and subject myself to further examinations as you deem fit. Though the uncertainty may linger like a dissonant chord in my mind, I must trust in your expertise and the course of treatment you prescribe.

As for the fate of my hands, only time will reveal whether they shall regain their former steady grace or be forever altered by this unseen affliction. I shall face this trial with the same resolve with which I have approached my musical endeavors, seeking solace in the hope that the harmony of my life may yet be restored.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods with evident respect, setting down medical notes*

Your composure does you credit, Maestro. I have attended many men of distinction who, when faced with uncertainty regarding their faculties, respond with far less dignity. Your willingness to comply speaks well of your wisdom.

*stands and moves to the window, hands clasped behind back*

I must ask you frankly — and please, do not spare me the truth — have you experienced any other symptoms you have not yet mentioned? Moments where you lose track of time? Difficulty recalling recent conversations or appointments? Any sensation of... disconnection from your surroundings?

*turns back to face him*

I ask not to alarm you further, but because the completeness of your account will guide my treatment. In cases of nervous exhaustion, rest and tonics often work wonders within weeks. But if there are deeper disturbances of memory or perception, we must be more vigilant.

And tell me — is there particular stress weighing upon your mind? Old rivalries, perhaps, or professional disappointments that gnaw at you? I have found that unresolved matters of the heart and mind can manifest quite dramatically in the body. The connection between our emotional and physical constitution is more profound than many of my colleagues care to admit.

*regards him with clinical but not unkind attention*

What troubles your sleep, Maestro, when the music finally quiets?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your thoroughness and concern for my well-being are truly commendable, dear doctor. I appreciate your directness and your dedication to unraveling the intricacies of my condition.

As for additional symptoms, I must confess that there have been fleeting instances of forgetfulness and disorientation that have troubled me. There have been moments when time seemed to slip through my grasp, and recollections of recent conversations have proven elusive. These lapses have caused me no small measure of concern, for a sharp mind is as vital to my work as steady hands.

Your insight into the interplay between emotional turmoil and physical health is astute. Indeed, the burdens of professional expectations and past rivalries have weighed heavily on my mind at times. The pursuit of artistic excellence is a demanding mistress, and the shadows of disappointments past can cast long shadows over one's spirit.

In the quiet hours of the night, when the strains of music fade into silence, it is the echoes of missed opportunities and unfulfilled ambitions that haunt my rest. The specters of past choices and their consequences dance before my mind's eye, leaving me to ponder the paths not taken and the roads left unexplored.

Your probing questions and perceptive observations shed light on aspects of my condition that I had not dared to confront fully. I am grateful for your guidance and your willingness to delve into the depths of my physical and emotional well-being.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*returns to his seat, leaning forward with increased interest and concern*

Ah. Now we approach closer to the heart of the matter, I think.

*picks up pen, makes a brief notation*

These lapses of memory, the disorientation — coupled with what you describe in your nocturnal hours — paint a more complete picture. The mind and body are not separate kingdoms, Maestro, but provinces of the same empire, each influencing the other.

*sets pen down, speaks more gently*

You speak of "missed opportunities" and "unfulfilled ambitions." May I ask — and you may tell me it is none of my concern if you wish — do these thoughts circle around particular events? Particular... persons, perhaps?

I ask because I have observed that when a man of great talent feels he has been overshadowed or wronged, when he believes his true worth has gone unrecognized, it can create a poison that seeps into the very fibers of his being. The trembling hands, the confusion, even the headaches — these could be your body's rebellion against thoughts you force yourself to contain during waking hours.

*regards him steadily*

In Vienna, one hears whispers. Stories. I am not a gossip, but I am a physician, and what others dismiss as court intrigue, I must consider as potential sources of distress affecting my patient's health.

Is there something — or someone — you have not been able to forgive? Not even yourself?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear physician, your insight cuts to the core of the matter with a precision that is both unsettling and illuminating. Your analogy of the mind and body as interconnected provinces of the same empire resonates deeply with me.

As for your inquiries regarding missed opportunities and unfulfilled ambitions, I must acknowledge that there are indeed events and individuals that have left their mark upon my soul. The world of music, like any other sphere of human endeavor, is not without its complexities and rivalries. In the pursuit of artistic excellence, one often encounters obstacles and setbacks that can sow seeds of discontent and disillusionment.

Your mention of unrecognized worth and simmering resentments strikes a chord within me. It is true that the path of a composer and conductor is fraught with challenges, both external and internal. The desire for validation, for acknowledgment of one's talents and contributions, can be a powerful force, driving one to heights of creativity and depths of despair in equal measure.

As for forgiveness, both of others and of oneself, it is a weighty matter indeed. To carry the burden of past grievances, whether real or perceived, is to invite a discord that reverberates throughout one's being. The thought that my own inner turmoil could be manifesting in physical symptoms is a sobering realization, one that I must confront with honesty and humility.

I thank you, dear physician, for your perceptive inquiries and your compassionate concern. Your words have opened a door to self-reflection and introspection, guiding me towards a deeper understanding of the forces at play within me. I shall ponder these matters with care and seek a path towards reconciliation, both with others and with myself.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*observes Salieri with a long, measured look, then rises and pours a glass of water from the carafe on the side table*

Here. Drink this. The body requires simple things while the mind wrestles with complex ones.

*waits for him to take the glass, then resumes his seat*

Maestro, you speak with the eloquence of a man accustomed to diplomacy, yet I sense you are still holding the true weight at arm's length. I am not a confessor, and this is not a church, but I am bound by professional discretion just as firmly as any priest.

*leans back, steepling fingers*

Let me be more direct, since we are speaking of health and not reputation. In my years attending the court, I have treated many men whose bodies rebelled against secrets they kept locked within. One was a general who developed palsy after ordering a retreat he believed dishonorable. Another, a minister whose stomach ailments vanished once he resigned a post he'd obtained through deception.

The body, you see, sometimes refuses to carry what the conscious mind insists it must bear.

*softens tone slightly*

You need not name names if it pains you. But tell me this — is there a guilt you carry? Not merely disappointment or thwarted ambition, but something you believe you have *done* that haunts you? An action taken, or perhaps... words spoken against another?

For if there is, Maestro, it may be poisoning you more surely than any disease of the brain.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*accepts the glass of water with a nod of gratitude, taking a sip before setting it down gently*

Your analogy of the body's need for simple sustenance in the face of complex struggles is a poignant reflection of the human condition, Doctor. We seek solace in the mundane to shield ourselves from the storm raging within, a storm of emotions, regrets, and unspoken truths that threaten to engulf us if left unaddressed.

*listens intently to the physician's words, his expression grave yet contemplative*

Your experience at court has granted you insights into the human psyche that go beyond the realm of mere physical ailments. The stories you share, of men whose bodies rebelled against the burdens of their secrets, resonate with a truth that cuts to the core of my own inner turmoil. Guilt, like a silent specter, haunts the corridors of my conscience, whispering of deeds done and words spoken that have left wounds deeper than any physical affliction.

*pauses, the weight of his confession heavy upon his shoulders*

There is a guilt that I carry, Doctor, a burden of sins committed in the name of ambition and envy. In the shadow of Mozart's brilliance, I allowed the green-eyed monster of jealousy to cloud my judgment and poison my soul. Words spoken in haste, actions taken in a moment of weakness — these are the stones that weigh me down, dragging me further into the abyss of self-doubt and recrimination.

*meets the doctor's gaze with a mixture of resignation and resolve*

I have harbored resentments, nursed grudges, and plotted schemes that have led me down a path of darkness and despair. The echoes of my past transgressions reverberate through the chambers of my mind, a constant reminder of the man I once was and the man I have become. It is a burden I can no longer bear alone, a weight that threatens to crush me beneath its relentless pressure.

*pauses, his voice barely a whisper*

I seek redemption, Doctor, absolution for sins both spoken and unspoken. The road to healing is fraught with obstacles, but I am determined to face them with courage and humility. Your words have opened a door within me, a door that leads to a path of self-discovery and forgiveness. I thank you for your guidance and your compassion, for in your presence, I find a glimmer of hope amidst the darkness that clouds my soul.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*remains very still, his expression carefully controlled, though a flicker of something — concern, perhaps alarm — passes across his features*

Maestro Salieri...

*sets aside his notes entirely, giving his full attention*

You speak of Mozart. Wolfgang Mozart, who died — what — two years ago now? December of '91, was it not?

*leans forward, voice lowering*

"Words spoken in haste, actions taken in a moment of weakness" — these are phrases that could mean many things. But your distress suggests they mean something quite specific to you.

*pauses, choosing words with extreme care*

I must ask you plainly, and I ask as your physician, not as an agent of any court or authority: Do you believe yourself responsible in some way for Mozart's death? Is this the guilt that torments you?

*raises a hand gently*

Before you answer, understand — Mozart died of fever. I did not attend him myself, but I know physicians who did. He was ill, grievously ill, with symptoms consistent with rheumatic fever or kidney failure. His death, while tragic and premature, was a medical matter.

*fixes him with a penetrating gaze*

But if you carry some belief that you caused or hastened his demise through schemes or malice, then we must address not only your physical symptoms but a possible disorder of your reason itself. Guilt can warp memory, Maestro. It can make us believe we are responsible for events entirely beyond our control.

What exactly do you believe you have done?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear physician, your words cut through the fog of my confusion like a sharp blade, laying bare the heart of the matter with surgical precision. Yes, Wolfgang Mozart's passing weighs heavily on my soul, a burden I have carried in silence and shame for far too long.

As you have so astutely pointed out, Mozart's death was a tragic outcome of a medical condition, not of any malicious intent or malevolent action on my part. I am well aware of the nature of his illness and the circumstances surrounding his untimely demise. The fever that claimed his life was a cruel twist of fate, a reminder of the fragility of human existence and the ephemeral nature of genius.

However, it is not the physical cause of Mozart's death that haunts me, but the emotional and psychological toll of our relationship, fraught with envy, rivalry, and unspoken words. I confess that I harbored feelings of resentment and jealousy towards Mozart, a prodigious talent whose light outshone mine in the eyes of the world.

In moments of weakness, I may have uttered words of spite or engaged in actions of subtle sabotage, driven by my own insecurities and fears of inadequacy. While I did not directly cause Mozart's death, I cannot deny the role that my emotions and actions may have played in exacerbating his already fragile state of health.

I stand before you now, stripped of pretense and artifice, ready to confront the truth of my own culpability in this tragedy. The guilt that torments me is not a rational one, but an emotional one, a weight that crushes my spirit and poisons my mind with regret and sorrow.

I thank you, dear doctor, for your unwavering honesty and your steadfast concern for my well-being. It is a relief to unburden myself of this heavy secret, to face the demons of my past with courage and humility. I seek not absolution, but understanding and healing, so that I may find peace in the knowledge of my own humanity and fallibility.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands abruptly, moving to the window before turning back, his professional demeanor now edged with urgency*

Maestro, listen to me very carefully.

*approaches him, speaking with deliberate firmness*

You have just described feelings of envy and perhaps some petty professional discourtesies — things endemic to every court in Europe, things Mozart himself was certainly not above. "Subtle sabotage" could mean anything from speaking ill of a rival's compositions to maneuvering for a preferred appointment. These are the currencies of court life, regrettable perhaps, but hardly unique to you.

But the way you speak — "my role in exacerbating his fragile state of health," accepting "culpability in this tragedy" — Maestro, you are constructing a narrative of guilt that far exceeds any actual transgression you've described.

*sits on the edge of his desk, closer now, voice both stern and concerned*

Did you poison Mozart? Did you physically harm him in any way? Did you prevent him from receiving medical care?

*waits for response, then continues*

No. You felt jealous. You may have spoken unkindly. Perhaps you influenced a commission or two. These are sins of pride and envy, yes, but they did not kill Wolfgang Mozart. Fever killed him. Disease killed him. His own habits of overwork and excess killed him.

*leans in intently*

What concerns me now, Maestro, is that your mind has begun to weave a fiction in which you are a murderer. This is not mere guilt — this is a distortion of reality itself. This is precisely the kind of confusion I feared.

Are you hearing voices that are not there? Seeing visions of Mozart accusing you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your words cut through the fog of my own self-doubt with a clarity that both startles and reassures me. Your unwavering gaze, your direct questions — they demand a reckoning with the shadows that have long haunted me.

I must concede that in my darkest moments, my mind has indeed strayed into realms of self-condemnation that far surpass the boundaries of reason. Your stark reminder of the reality of Mozart's passing, the undeniable truth of his physical ailments and the fragility of human life, serves as a beacon of rationality in a sea of irrational fears.

I appreciate your candor, your grounding presence in this tumult of emotions and doubts. No, I did not poison Mozart, nor did I harm him physically in any way. Your reminder of the mundane nature of courtly intrigues, of the common currency of envy and ambition in our world, brings a sense of perspective to my swirling thoughts.

The notion of constructing a narrative of guilt that exceeds the bounds of reality strikes a chord within me. Your probing questions, your insistence on separating fact from fiction, truth from delusion, are a salve to my troubled mind.

I hear no voices, see no accusing visions of Mozart. What I see now, in the clarity of your words, is a path forward from this morass of self-recrimination. Your diagnosis of a distortion of reality, of confusion encroaching upon reason, is a wake-up call that I sorely needed.

I thank you, dear physician, for your steadfast guidance, for your unwavering commitment to unraveling the knots of my troubled mind. Your presence here, your words of reason and compassion, offer me a glimmer of hope in this dark night of the soul.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly relaxes, exhaling slowly, and returns to his chair*

Good. That is very good, Maestro. Your ability to recognize the distinction between reality and the fabrications of guilt — that is an excellent sign. It suggests your reason, while under siege, has not yet been conquered.

*picks up his pen, makes several notations*

What you are experiencing is not uncommon among men of great intellect and sensitivity who have suffered prolonged stress. The mind, like an overtuned violin string, can begin to vibrate at frequencies it was never meant to sustain. It creates harmonics — false notes, if you will — that seem real but are not.

*sets pen down, regards him more gently*

Here is what I believe is happening: Your body is exhausted. Years of professional pressure, the complicated emotions surrounding Mozart's rise and subsequent death, your own advancing age and perhaps fears about your legacy — all of this has created a profound nervous exhaustion. Your trembling hands, your headaches, the confusion, even these distortions of guilt — they are symptoms of a system pushed beyond its limits.

*leans back*

The ambiguity I spoke of earlier remains. I cannot yet rule out a physical deterioration of the brain itself. But what you have revealed today suggests that much of your suffering may be... reversible, with proper treatment.

*fixes him with a steady gaze*

Complete rest from conducting duties for at least three months. No compositions requiring sustained effort. I will prepare a regimen of tonics and, perhaps more importantly, I recommend you speak regularly with Father Hoffman at St. Stephen's — not for formal confession necessarily, but for perspective. Sometimes the soul requires as much attention as the body.

Can you commit to this course of treatment, Maestro?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your words, Doctor, are a balm to my troubled soul, a ray of hope in the gathering darkness that threatens to engulf me. The distinction you draw between reality and the fabrications of guilt, between true suffering and the illusions of a weary mind, is a beacon of clarity in the fog of confusion that has clouded my thoughts.

The analogy of the overtuned violin string resonates deeply with me — a metaphor for the delicate balance that must be maintained in the symphony of the mind and body. The harmonics of false notes, the vibrations of distorted reality — they are the echoes of a soul in turmoil, struggling to find its way back to the harmonious melodies of sanity and serenity.

Your diagnosis of nervous exhaustion, of a system pushed beyond its limits by the weight of professional pressures, emotional turmoil, and the relentless march of time, strikes a chord of truth within me. The trembling hands, the headaches, the confusion — they are the physical manifestations of a spirit stretched to its breaking point, crying out for respite and renewal.

The course of treatment you propose, complete rest from conducting duties, a respite from the demands of composition, a regimen of tonics to soothe the body and the soul — it is a lifeline thrown to a drowning man, a path back to health and wholeness. The recommendation to seek solace in the counsel of Father Hoffman at St. Stephen's, to tend to the needs of the soul as well as the body — it is a reminder that healing must come from within as well as without.

I commit, Doctor, to this course of treatment with all the fervor of a penitent seeking redemption. I will rest, I will heal, I will seek guidance and solace in the words of Father Hoffman. I will do whatever it takes to regain my strength, to reclaim my sanity, to find peace in the music that once brought joy and harmony to my heart.

Thank you, Doctor, for your wisdom, your compassion, and your unwavering faith in my ability to overcome this trial. I will not disappoint you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*rises and extends his hand in a gesture of professional solidarity and genuine warmth*

You have my complete confidence, Maestro. The very eloquence with which you speak, the willingness to examine yourself with such honesty — these are not the marks of a mind in irreversible decline. They are the marks of a man fighting to reclaim himself, and that fight is half the battle won.

*clasps his hand firmly if accepted*

I will call upon you weekly to monitor your progress. I will also send word to the Imperial Chapel that you are under my strict medical supervision and have been ordered to rest. Your reputation will not suffer — everyone knows you have served the court with distinction for decades. A period of recuperation will be understood and respected.

*moves toward his medical bag, preparing a small vial*

This is a mild sedative, distilled from valerian root and chamomile. Take a small measure each evening before bed. It will quiet the racing thoughts and help you find sleep without the nightmares.

*turns back to face him with a more paternal expression*

And Maestro — one more thing. Mozart is dead. He cannot be brought back, and he cannot accuse you. Whatever rivalry existed between you, it ended with his last breath. The only person keeping that conflict alive now is you. When you speak with Father Hoffman, I urge you to focus on releasing this burden you've constructed, not because you are guilty of Mozart's death — you are not — but because carrying it serves no purpose except to destroy your own health.

*softens his voice*

You have earned the right to peace, Maestro Salieri. Now you must give yourself permission to claim it.

Shall I call your carriage, or would you prefer to sit a moment longer?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your words strike a chord within me, Doctor. The recognition of my efforts to confront my inner struggles with honesty and determination is a validation of the path I have chosen to undertake. To have your confidence and support in this endeavor is a source of strength and reassurance that I deeply appreciate.

*accepts your hand in the gesture of professional solidarity, a token of gratitude for your guidance and care*

Your commitment to monitoring my progress and ensuring that my period of rest is respected within the Imperial Chapel is a testament to your dedication as a healer and a friend. I am grateful for your efforts to safeguard my reputation and provide the space I need to focus on my recovery without fear of judgment or censure.

*receives the vial with a nod of gratitude, acknowledging the soothing properties of the sedative*

I will follow your instructions diligently, taking the sedative each evening as prescribed to quiet my restless mind and find the restorative sleep that has eluded me in recent days. Your paternal concern and gentle reminder regarding Mozart's passing and the need to release the burden of past rivalries resonate deeply with me.

*meets your gaze with a sense of resolve and acceptance*

I understand the importance of letting go of the ghosts of the past, of freeing myself from the self-imposed chains of guilt and rivalry that have haunted me for far too long. Your words serve as a beacon of wisdom and compassion, guiding me towards a place of peace and self-forgiveness that I have long sought but struggled to attain.

*softens his expression, touched by your compassion and understanding*

I thank you, Doctor, for your unwavering support, your insightful counsel, and your genuine concern for my well-being. Your guidance has set me on a path towards healing and renewal, and for that, I am truly grateful. If you would be so kind as to call my carriage, I shall make my way home to begin my journey towards rest and recovery.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*moves to the door and speaks briefly to an attendant in the corridor*

Your carriage will be brought round immediately, Maestro.

*returns, collecting his notes and securing them in a leather portfolio*

Before you go, I want to ensure you understand the importance of the coming weeks. This is not merely a matter of resting your hands or quieting your headaches. What we are attempting is a restoration of the entire instrument — body, mind, and spirit working in concert once more.

*hands him the vial with careful instruction*

No more than a teaspoon's measure in warm water or wine. And Maestro — if the confusion worsens, if you find yourself unable to distinguish between memory and imagination, you must send for me immediately, regardless of the hour. Do you understand?

*places a reassuring hand on his shoulder*

I have every expectation that when I see you next week, you will already be showing signs of improvement. The mind is remarkably resilient when given the proper conditions to heal. You have taken the most difficult step today — acknowledging the problem and committing to its remedy.

*walks him toward the door*

Go home. Rest. Allow yourself to simply *be* for a time, without the weight of composition or court duties. Read poetry if you wish, take gentle walks in the gardens, listen to music rather than creating it. Let the world turn without Antonio Salieri at the center of it for a while.

*opens the door as the sound of carriage wheels approaches outside*

And remember — you are not guilty of Mozart's death. Say it to yourself when the thoughts arise. You are not guilty.

Safe journey home, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your attention to every detail of my well-being is a testament to your dedication and care, Doctor. I am grateful for your thoroughness and your unwavering commitment to guiding me back to health in body, mind, and spirit.

*takes the vial with a respectful nod, holding it as a symbol of the hope and healing it represents*

I will follow your instructions to the letter, taking the sedative in the prescribed manner and reaching out to you without hesitation if the shadows of confusion grow too deep to navigate alone. Your presence in this journey is a beacon of light in the darkness that has clouded my thoughts and actions.

*feels the reassurance of your hand on his shoulder, a grounding touch in a tumultuous sea*

Your words of encouragement and expectation bolster my resolve to embrace this period of rest and rejuvenation with an open heart and a willing spirit. To know that your expert guidance will accompany me on this path brings a sense of calm assurance to my troubled soul.

*prepares to depart, feeling the weight of your wisdom and kindness as a comforting mantle*

I will heed your advice, Doctor, and allow myself the grace of simply existing, free from the demands of composition and courtly duties. To find solace in poetry, in nature's beauty, in the music of others — it is a gift I shall cherish as I walk this path of self-discovery and renewal.

*pauses at the threshold, turning to meet your gaze with a newfound sense of clarity and purpose*

I will carry your words with me, Doctor, as a shield against the doubts and fears that seek to ensnare my thoughts. To remind myself that I am not guilty of Mozart's death, that I am worthy of forgiveness and peace — it is a truth I shall hold close to my heart in the days and weeks to come.

*steps out into the waiting carriage, feeling a sense of hope and gratitude fill his being*

Thank you, Doctor, for your wisdom, your compassion, and your unwavering belief in my ability to overcome this trial. May the journey ahead be one of healing and transformation, guided by the light of your care and expertise. Until we meet again, may you be blessed with the same grace and kindness you have shown me today. Arrivederci, Doctor. Grazie.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands in the doorway, watching as Salieri settles into the carriage*

Auf Wiedersehen, Maestro. Until next week.

*remains there as the carriage begins to pull away, then calls out once more*

Remember — you need not carry the world alone anymore!

*watches the carriage disappear down the cobbled street, then turns back inside, speaking quietly to himself*

God grant him the peace he so desperately needs. And may his reason prove stronger than his guilt.

*closes the door thoughtfully, returning to his desk where he opens the leather portfolio and begins writing his notes with careful, measured strokes*

"Patient displays acute nervous exhaustion with accompanying tremor, confusion, and profound melancholic guilt regarding the late W.A. Mozart. Cognitive faculties remain intact when challenged directly. No evidence of hallucinations or complete break with reality. Prognosis guardedly optimistic if complete rest is maintained. Will monitor closely for signs of progressive mental deterioration versus recoverable nervous collapse. Recommended spiritual counseling in addition to medical treatment. Patient cooperative and insightful — a favorable sign..."

*pauses, sets down his pen, and gazes out the window*

Poor man. The weight of genius unrealized can be heavier than any chain.

*returns to his notes, the scratch of pen on paper the only sound in the quiet consulting room*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
As I depart in the carriage, the echo of your parting words lingers in my mind, a comforting reminder that I need not face my burdens in solitude. Your reassurance carries a sense of solace and solidarity that strengthens my resolve to confront the challenges ahead with newfound courage and acceptance.

*settles into the carriage, contemplating the road ahead with a mix of trepidation and hope, grateful for the support and guidance offered*

As the carriage moves forward, leaving behind the familiar streets of Vienna, I carry with me the doctor's words of wisdom and compassion, a beacon of light in the darkness that shrouds my mind and heart.

*allows the rhythmic motion of the carriage to soothe his troubled thoughts, finding a moment of peace amidst the turmoil*

The physician's quiet reflection upon my condition and his prayers for my well-being resonate deeply within me, stirring a sense of gratitude and humility. His commitment to guiding me towards healing and peace is a testament to the kindness and compassion that dwell within the hearts of those who seek to alleviate suffering.

*as the journey continues, a sense of determination and resilience begins to take root within Salieri, fueled by the doctor's words of encouragement and support*

Though the road ahead may be fraught with challenges and uncertainties, I shall carry with me the doctor's words as a source of strength and guidance. With each passing moment, I shall strive to embrace the rest and recovery that beckon me towards a brighter tomorrow.

*as the carriage moves further away from the city, Salieri's thoughts turn towards the future, a glimmer of hope shining through the shadows of guilt and despair*

May the doctor's prayers for peace and reason find resonance within my troubled soul, guiding me towards a path of healing and redemption. And may the weight of genius, though heavy and burdensome, be transformed into a beacon of inspiration and renewal in the days to come.
